NIDA says it has registered 27,520,835 people and issued 23,515,667 National Identification Numbers; the registered count is about 39 percent of the 70.5 million population held (2025), calculated here.

Home Affairs minister Patrobas Katambi reported 27,520,835 people registered with NIDA and 23,515,667 issued a National Identification Number, which is 39% and 33% of the 70.5 million population (shares computed from the population held; figures as corrected in the record's summary, the body text differing).

Over 22 million Tanzanians held a National Identification Number as of April 2026, per an FSDT analysis; against 70.5 million people this is about 31 percent or a little more (derived, 'over' is a lower bound).

NIDA reports 27.1 million adults registered (87% adult coverage) and shows 50.8% of the population excluded because children are deferred, which leaves under two-thirds of the whole population registered.
The release says Jamii Namba has registered over 25 million people, and Co-Develop describes Tanzania as a country of over 60 million people.
